item.title: Finland at the Olympics: Kärävä into slopestyle final, Lehto 15th
item.description: Finland opened its second full day of competition at the Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics with mixed results as Anni Kärävä secured a place in the women’s freeski slopestyle final and Elian Lehto fell short of expectations in the men’s downhill. Kärävä advanced to Monday’s final after qualifying inside the top 12 despite a fall on her second run. Lehto placed 15th in Bormio, more than two seconds behind the winner, after a run that failed to match his early-season form.

item.title: Orpo confirms willingness to continue as National Coalition leader
item.description: Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on Saturday that he is ready to continue as leader of Finland’s National Coalition Party as it prepares for its summer party congress, where his tenure will reach nearly ten years. Orpo made the announcement during the party’s leadership days in Helsinki, where he delivered a policy address focused on the economy, public finances, and security. item.title: Major fire destroys Jokioinen Leipä bread factory
item.description: A fire destroyed the main bakery of Jokioinen Leipä bread factory in the municipality of Jokioinen in southern Finland early on Sunday morning. The blaze broke out shortly after 4.30am at the company’s factory on Leivänkuja. Flames spread through the structure and reached the roof. Rescue services fought the fire through the morning. Authorities said the building will be lost. The bakery stood empty at the time of the fire. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Snowfall and shifting temperatures ahead after prolonged cold
item.description: A prolonged spell of cold and dry winter weather across Finland is set to give way to more variable conditions during the week beginning 9 February, according to meteorologists from Foreca and the Finnish Meteorological Institute. High pressure that has dominated the country for weeks is moving south. In its wake, cloud cover and snowfall increase across large parts of Finland. Night-time temperatures remain low, while daytime conditions turn more unsettled.

item.title: Lindsey Vonn undergoes surgery after Olympic downhill fall
item.description: Lindsey Vonn underwent surgery on a fractured left leg after a heavy crash during the women’s downhill final at the Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics on Sunday, with doctors confirming her condition is stable. The 41-year-old American skier fell just 13 seconds into her run on the Olimpia delle Tofane course in Cortina d’Ampezzo. item.title: Asko and Sotka owner files for bankruptcy in Finland
item.description: Indoor Group, the owner of Finnish furniture chains Asko and Sotka, has filed for bankruptcy after prolonged financial distress and failed funding negotiations. The company confirmed on Monday that the bankruptcy application was submitted to the court the same day. Its subsidiary, sofa manufacturer Insofa, filed a separate application at the same time. Indoor Group said attempts to secure financing through corporate arrangements continued for months.

item.title: Sweden plans to tighten citizenship rules
item.description: Sweden’s centre-right government plans to tighten the rules for acquiring citizenship, raising residence requirements and introducing stricter tests and income limits. The proposal extends the minimum period of residence from five years to eight. Applicants must also demonstrate knowledge of the Swedish language and an understanding of Swedish society. Migration Minister Johan Forssell said the changes mark a clear shift from existing practice.

item.title: Lindsey Vonn undergoes second surgery after Olympic crash
item.description: Lindsey Vonn has undergone two surgical procedures on her left leg following a serious crash during the women’s downhill at the Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics, according to sources cited by Reuters and La Repubblica. The 41-year-old American skier suffered a major fracture after falling around 13 seconds into her run on Sunday. The crash ended her attempt to win another Olympic medal despite racing with a fully ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in her left knee.

item.title: Finland’s asylum reform criticised over human rights risks
item.description: A major reform of Finland’s asylum and migration system faces criticism from the Deaconess Foundation, which says the planned national implementation of the EU migration and asylum pact weakens legal safeguards and threatens equal treatment. item.title: Finnish household share investments reach record high in 2025
item.description: Finnish households recorded strong gains from share investments during 2025 as rising prices of domestic equities lifted portfolio values to the highest level on record. Data published by the Bank of Finland show that household share investments generated a total return of 29.9 per cent during the year, including price changes and dividend income. The total value of household shareholdings reached 59.0 billion euros at the end of December, exceeding all previous peaks.
